title: Site Coverage of Vending Services Program Agreements
content:
A client may hold a Vending Services Program agreement at as many sites as it has, and there is no ceiling on the number held at once. Each agreement is written against exactly one site, and machines, sales, commission and statements belong to that site's agreement alone. A further vending agreement is not opened for a site that already carries an open vending agreement, so a site carries at most 1 open vending agreement at any moment. A site's agreement counts as open while it is proposed, active or suspended, and counts as gone once it is closed. Where a client wants more machines at a site already under agreement, the machine count on the existing agreement is raised rather than a second agreement opened.

### What the register admits, and on whose word

Before a vending agreement is opened, the client and the site it is to stand at are read off the register of vending agreements held. The register is the authority on whether that site already carries an open agreement; the client's own account of what they hold at the site does not settle it, and the check is made on the pairing of client and site rather than on the client alone. An agreement standing proposed, active or suspended at that pairing is an open agreement for this purpose. Where the register shows such an agreement, a further agreement is not opened for that site.

### The rule set out as a matrix

| What the register shows at this client and this site | May a further vending agreement be opened for the site |
| --- | --- |
| An agreement standing proposed | no |
| An agreement standing active | no |
| An agreement standing suspended | no |
| An agreement standing closed, and no other open agreement | yes |
| No vending agreement at all | yes |

### Cases at the boundary of the rule (hypothetical clients)

A client holding an active Vending Services Program agreement at a warehouse and asking for a vending bank at a separate head office site is within the rule, because the ceiling on sites held at once is not there: the second site takes its own agreement, and its machines, sales, commission and statements belong to it alone. The same client asking for a second agreement at the warehouse, where the active agreement already stands, is not: what the warehouse wants is a higher machine count on the agreement it already holds. A client whose only agreement at a site closed last quarter is in the third position, since a closed agreement is gone from the site and a fresh agreement may be written there.
